description: We are TukTuk Intergaláctico, a team of Systems Engineering students from Guatemala passionate about technology, innovation, and solving real-world problems. We enjoy programming, exploring new technologies, and turning creative ideas into practical solutions. Our goal is to combine teamwork, curiosity, and technical skills to create an innovative project using NASA's open data. We're ready to take Guatemalan creativity beyond Earth!
summary: ARES PATH is an interactive Marswalk planning prototype focused on Jezero Crater. It combines a documented NASA/USGS HiRISE elevation dataset with aligned HiRISE optical imagery and NASA Mars Trek CTX/HiRISE visual context. Users select an analysis area and two grid cells, then the FastAPI backend calculates two explainable route alternatives: a shortest traversable route and a terrain-aware route that accounts for elevation-derived slope. The interface displays both paths, physical metrics, an elevation profile, data provenance, and limitations so users can understand how terrain changes a planning decision. A browser-based Mission Pack can be exported, imported, and reviewed offline with the saved response, profile, and compact preview; live NASA layers and new route calculations remain online-only. ARES PATH is not certified astronaut navigation or safety guidance. It demonstrates how layered NASA data could support future human explorers before a Marswalk.
details:
ARES PATH is an interactive research prototype for explainable Marswalk route planning in Jezero Crater. It addresses the challenge by combining NASA Mars terrain data, orbital imagery, and Mars Trek visual context in one map-based workflow.

The user selects an active regional dataset, defines an analysis area, and chooses an origin and destination using raster grid cells. The backend validates that both points are inside the dataset, have valid elevation values, and satisfy the selected terrain constraints. It then calculates two route alternatives using A* search: a shortest traversable route and a terrain-aware route that accounts for elevation-derived slope. Instead of presenting one opaque answer, ARES PATH shows both routes, distance, ascent, descent, slope information, expanded cells, an elevation profile, data provenance, and structured error messages.

The frontend was built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, OpenLayers, and reusable component architecture. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, Rasterio, NumPy, and deterministic geospatial routing services. Processed GeoTIFF datasets are validated through CRS, transform, shape, extent, and checksum metadata.

ARES PATH also supports browser-based Mission Packs that can be saved, exported, imported, and reviewed offline. Offline mode preserves the mission response, profile, and compact preview; new route calculations and live NASA layers require an internet connection.

The project is designed as a transparent research prototype, not certified astronaut navigation or safety guidance. Its main contribution is making terrain trade-offs, data sources, assumptions, and limitations visible to future mission planners.
